title: Fibrations and weak equivalences of quasicategories in the Joyal model structure
statement: Use quasicategories, inner horns, equivalence edges, functor simplicial sets and functor equivalences as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Use the Joyal model structure and its classes of fibrations and weak equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. For any two quasicategories $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ in the same universe and any simplicial functor $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, the following characterizations hold. (1) The map $f$ is a Joyal fibration if and only if it has the right lifting property against every inner horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, and, for every vertex $c\in\mathcal C$ and equivalence edge $e:f(c)\to d$ in $\mathcal D$, there is an equivalence edge $\widetilde e:c\to\widetilde d$ in $\mathcal C$ with $f(\widetilde e)=e$. (2) The map $f$ is a Joyal weak equivalence if and only if it has a simplicial quasi-inverse $g:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ and coherent natural equivalences between $gf$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and between $fg$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D}$, where these are equivalence edges in the corresponding functor quasicategories. In (2) the Joyal weak equivalences are exactly the categorical equivalences defined by the tests $h\operatorname{Fun}(-,\mathcal E)$ in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure].
